data.description:
Placeholder for the empirical-verification pillar of the test creation calibration North Star. Sibling to d566-afa6 (gen-time prevention), 7f42-e41f (growth metrics), 69e8-af39 (feedback loop).

Goal: provide an execution-time signal that a candidate test would catch a real regression by verifying it kills at least one behavior-changing mutant injected into the changed lines on the diff. This is the strongest catch-power signal in the test-quality literature and is the upstream complement to d566-afa6's write-time articulation gate (Tier 1 + Tier 2): mutation-kill verification is Tier 3.

## Research synthesis (to refine via /dso:brainstorm)

**Why mutation kill on the changed line.** Just et al. (FSE 2014, on Defects4J) showed mutation detection correlates with real-fault detection independently of coverage; Papadakis et al. (2018, 2019) refined that the correlation is weak overall but significantly stronger at the high end. Translation: mutation score is unusable as a graded quality score, but usable as a high-threshold filter on the specific lines a test claims to cover. Inozemtseva & Holmes (ICSE 2014) ruled out line/branch coverage as a quality signal for the same diff. Meta's 2025 Mutation-Guided LLM Test Generation paper (FSE 2025, follow-up to TestGen-LLM 2024) is the published state-of-the-art for exactly this problem class: generate -> keep only tests that kill at least one injected mutant in the diff.

**Tooling landscape — what to pilot.**
- JS/TS: Stryker with --incremental + scoped mutate globs. Mutates only changed regions; 70-90% faster on PRs; published stryker-mutator/github-action with break thresholds. Most pre-commit-viable tool surveyed.
- Python: mutmut (boxed/mutmut). ~1,200 mutants/min, AST-based, actively maintained. Cosmic-ray is slower and less active.
- Java: PIT 1.19.x scmMutationCoverage — runs only on diffed files. Trendyol et al. gate via SonarQube quality gates. JVM-locked.
- C++: mull. LLVM-IR based; fast (compile-once); active across LLVM 13-22.
- Go: go-gremlins (preferred) or avito-tech fork of go-mutesting.
- Ruby: mutant. Maintained but smaller community.

**Cost reality.** Even with incremental modes, none of these are <5s/file in practice on real diffs. Mainstream adoption is nightly audits, not pre-commit gates. The Tier 3 design must decide whether mutation runs (a) pre-commit synchronously, (b) post-commit asynchronously with a report channel, (c) on the PR after llm-review, or (d) nightly with regression-detection feedback.

**Property-based testing surprise** (cross-relevant, may warrant a follow-on or split). OOPSLA 2025 (Coblenz et al.): each Hypothesis property finds ~50x more mutants than the average example-based unit test, with >50% of caught mutants killable by a single input. If Tier 3 is fundamentally about catch-power per test, property-based testing is a candidate primary intervention rather than an afterthought. To be evaluated in brainstorm.

## Dependencies and ordering

d566-afa6 (Tier 1 + Tier 2 gen-time prevention) ships first and stands alone — it provides the write-time floor and the intent-claim articulation that this epic verifies empirically. This epic adds the execution-time verification on top of d566's claim manifest: 'the test that claims to verify SC X must actually kill a mutant on the code that implements SC X.'

## Open questions for brainstorm

- Polyglot mutation infrastructure scope (one-shot pilot in a single language, or full polyglot from day one?)
- Where in the pipeline (pre-commit, post-commit, PR-gate, nightly)
- How to map mutant-kill back to the intent-claim manifest from d566-afa6 (mutant on file F kills test T claiming SC X — does that confirm T verifies X, or do we need stronger evidence?)
- Property-based testing — primary intervention or sibling effort

## Out of scope (other siblings)
- d566-afa6: write-time prevention of change-detector tests via assertion-shape rules + intent-claim articulation
- 7f42-e41f: suite-growth-vs-behavioral-coverage metrics
- 69e8-af39: production-bug / review-finding feedback loop
- c13f-6196: post-hoc detection of irrelevant test->source mappings

Refine via /dso:brainstorm.
data.title: Test creation calibration (d): mutation-testing infrastructure for empirical test-catch-power verification
